elements.element: Customer is not subject to any most-favoured-nation obligation in Vendor's favour.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer has no obligation to offer Vendor terms no less favourable than Customer's best terms for another technology supplier. Section 12.3 further confirms that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer is limited to a defined product.
elements.evidence: The condition for this limitation is demonstrably absent: the rendered clause imposes no MFN obligation on Customer, so no broader product scope applies.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer is limited to 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition for this duration requirement is demonstrably absent because Section 7.2 negates the MFN obligation entirely.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer includes reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: The condition for requiring comparison carve-outs is demonstrably absent because Customer has no operative MFN obligation.

result.reason: The redline directly negates the MFN obligation that previously burdened Customer, while leaving the unrelated provisions intact. It does not prevent voluntary or Customer-favourable MFN pricing. Because no Customer-burdening MFN remains, the fallback limitations are satisfied without needing product, duration, or comparison language.
